claimRules: "Needs no supervisor" does not mean simpler, cheaper or more reliable. Each of those is a separate claim that needs its own evidence, or it is not made.
A result that holds only at one setting of the rival's assumptions is stated with that setting, never as a general claim.
A claim about locality names its failure model: per crash or per process (`bench/PREREG.md` §6).
The fairness rules (`bench/REPORT.md` §1) are never revisited to rescue a result.
Replay proves that this code produces the recorded run from the recorded model outputs. It does not prove where those outputs came from. Say exactly that.

R1.text: Recovery stays local to the affected subtree.

R2.text: Resilience comparable to an ideal durable supervisor, without a central coordinator or a separate recovery mechanism.

R3.text: The conditions, stated next to R2: against `durable-max` on T2 at C3, locality holds when the supervisor needs 1–3 s more to restart a coordinator (coordinator-dependency time 0.28 and 0.19 of the supervisor's); it ties at the default assumptions (both detect a failure in 5 s, no extra restart) and when both detect in 1–10 s; it fails when an external supervisor detects and restarts within 0.5–1 s while the swarm keeps its 5 s detection (13.2 and 5.7 times the supervisor's). Per process, each coordinator process failing at the same rate, the two are comparable (ratio 0.90), and the supervisor recovers sooner. The swarm's failure detector also produces false deaths (1.25–2.25 per run at C2–C3), the supervisors none.

R4.status: allowed with its setting (Oct 30). The 10-seed extension re-reads it before the video or the README use it; whatever it shows is reported
R4.text: On the real model, at the headline point (T2, C3: five coordinator crashes, half the agents killed), recovery stayed local: the swarm's coordinator-dependency time, blast radius and idle agent-seconds were below half of `durable-max`'s on every seed.

R5.text: Against an in-process supervisor, whose workers die with it, the swarm at C3 stalled 8.2 s (T1) and 14.6 s (T2) against 62.6 and 92.6 s, with +2.6% and +6.6% extra cost against +37.7% and +75.6%.

R6.text: On the real model, with five of its ten coordinators crashed and half its agents killed, every run finished with a valid result. It stalled 14.6 s against 92.6 s for an in-process supervisor, and tied an ideal durable supervisor.

S1.status: allowed by construction; pending the recorded check on the final bundle
S1.text: No separate recovery mechanism: every survivor computes the same heir from the log with one rule (HRW), so there is no election.

S2.text: Any orchestrator can die mid-run, the root included, and the run still finishes.

S3.text: No process manager, standby or election service.

S4.status: allowed as a property of the design, never as an advantage over the rivals
S4.text: Zero LLM tokens spent on coordination.

S5.text: Every run replays bit-for-bit from a hash-verified log; `fractalswarm demo --verify` needs no API key.

S7.status: allowed. The measured numbers go under it as a subtitle, each with its rival named (R2, R3), never as part of the tagline
S7.text: The tagline: "Kill half the brains. It still finishes." Only that sentence (Yoel, Oct 30).
